The node's owner cuts the link from the UI; the runtime is left alone (spec §5.2).
SHA-256 of the certificate the panel at `url` presents, for pin-on-trust (spec §4).
Heartbeat and delivery for this node now, not on the next tick.

delete.description:
`?force=1` is the owner's override for a node that is gone for good: provisioned
grants the node never confirmed deleting are abandoned (audited as such).

get.description:
The node's runtime users per protocol, each with the grant this panel already
holds for it (`linked_grant_id`), so the import step can offer only the rest.

post.description: v0.11: the central asks the node's agent to poll upstream (`versions.check`).

get.description:
What the central wants the node to run and what the node last reported: numbers,
digests and per-resource states — credentials travel by reference only.

post.description:
v0.11: ask the agent to poll upstream; an agent error travels as it does for
an update (the global `VersionAgentError` handler).

The managers a panel update left pending (`pending_rebuild`) are rebuilt by the
agent in the background; a running update answers 409 (the global handler).

get.description:
v0.15: the overview's resource card alone, cheap enough to poll every few seconds
(`/api/dashboard` asks every protocol runtime as well).

post.description: The configuration of the key the panel keeps: nothing on the node changes.
Adopt every grant of one protocol that still has no stored credential.
The name one access carries in subscriptions (presentation only).

One grant, local or on a linked panel; a remote change only records what the
central wants and the pusher delivers it (the reply never carries a credential).

One reveal for every artifact of the operation, rendered from escrow, each grant
with the public hosts of the node it lives on.

Every link the client can be handed right now, rebuilt from escrow, with a QR for
each of them: MTProxy has no subscription a client could poll, so this is how that
access is given out — at issue time and every time after it. `grant_id` asks for
one grant only: the window of a single access shows its own link and nothing else.

delete.description: Permanent removal of an archived client that has no grants left.

get.description: Subscription and node events, oldest first, paged by row id; every role may read them.

This panel's own clients of one protocol with their current rates: the protocol pages
paint them next to each user. `live` is false for NaiveProxy (rows from finished connections).

EgressDocument.title: EgressDocument
EgressDocument.description:
What one protocol's egress should be on the node (v0.4, spec §8.3): the compiled
document the manager validates, named by the policy revision it came from.

With the node's Xray-router (v0.5) a section names *two* managers: `backend` says
which one `document` is for (the router's intent under `xray_router`, the native
manager's document otherwise) and `companion` is what the *other* one gets afterwards
— the native attach document beside a router intent, the router's pass-through beside a
native detach. Absent from the wire when None, so a v0.4 node keeps its strict model.

ExitInput.title: ExitInput
ExitInput.description:
What `POST /api/routing/exits` and the link importer produce; on an update a missing
`credential` keeps the escrowed one.

ExplainBody.title: ExplainBody
ExplainBody.description: «Куда пойдёт…» (v0.7): a host or address and a port, walked through the lane's rules.

LaneModeBody.title: LaneModeBody
LaneModeBody.description: A grant's routing lane (v0.7): the service's, or its own.

NodeLinkUpdate.title: NodeLinkUpdate
NodeLinkUpdate.description: Only the fields given change; `allow_private_address` stays what it was at link time.

NodeVersionUpdate.title: NodeVersionUpdate
NodeVersionUpdate.description: `{version, expected_current}` for one component of a linked panel; the component is in the path.

PolicyInput.title: PolicyInput
PolicyInput.description:
What `PUT` accepts: the intent without the server's bookkeeping. `backend` may be
left out — the policy keeps the backend it has (its native one at birth) — but a named
one must be one the protocol can run on (`backends_for`).

PolicyPut.title: PolicyPut
PolicyPut.description: The policy plus the revision the operator edited; None on a first save.

RelayAccount.title: RelayAccount
RelayAccount.description:
One account of the node's relay inbound: the source node and its exit in the email
(`relay:<source guid>:<direct|warp>`), the UUID in the push's secrets by this ref.

RelaySection.title: RelaySection
RelaySection.description:
The node's relay inbound (v0.7, spec §7): vless+reality on `port` with the node's own
panel name as the cover, and the accounts other nodes dial it with. `enabled: false`
takes the inbound down. The keypair is the node's; only its public part comes back.

RoutingRule.title: RoutingRule
RoutingRule.description:
One first-match rule. `id` is the server's; a rule sent without one is new.
`position` is the order the server stored — on input the list order wins.

RuleMatch.title: RuleMatch
RuleMatch.description:
What a rule matches: any of its domains, geosite codes, CIDRs or geoip codes, on any
of its ports. A rule may stand on ports alone (the router enforces it; native backends
say `unsupported`).
